content:
Rejecting a biological blueprint does not forbid biological insight
The author explicitly credits studying neuroanatomy while asserting that an artificial intelligence should look nothing like a human brain. That strong architectural conclusion needs criteria for what resemblance means and evidence about which mechanisms are useful. Rejecting literal duplication of a brain does not establish that every important resemblance is undesirable.

quote: chalk this up to the anthropic principle
content:
The selection caveat should govern the whole memoir
Acknowledging survivorship bias is a real strength. A good outcome after a mistaken belief does not show that the belief was a good policy, and a persuasive story from the person who persisted does not show what happened to comparable people who chose differently. Keep that caveat when the book later recruits this history as a route to exceptional competence.

quote: all reasoning on that level is something that can’t be trusted
content:
Operational knowledge can precede a deep theory
The author allows preliminary descriptions while warning against putting weight on informal reasoning. That warning is sensible when untested mechanisms carry the conclusion, but reliability can also be established within a tested range before a complete explanation exists. Precision helps expose assumptions; neither a formal definition nor a deep theory is an automatic certificate of truth.
